about: Adjudication of the outside errata meta-verification (PR 63). Each card tests one finding: the errata row's claim that the printed text is wrong. error_real is the adjudicated truth (true: the printed text is wrong; false: it was right; null: can't tell from the repo). errata_finding scores the errata row against it: a row that is not rejected asserts an error (positive), a rejected row asserts none (negative); true positive and true negative are valid findings, a false positive is a type I error (an error reported that isn't there), a false negative is a type II error (a real error missed), and unsettled means error_real is null. finding_valid is true for a valid finding, false for a type I or II error, null when unsettled. bo3_finding scores the Bo3 majority the same way, reading the checkers' labels as the prompt defined them: matches means the printed text is right (negative); disagrees, missing, superseded or impossible mean it is wrong (positive); can't tell or a three-way split is no call. Where claim_states_error is true, the card's claim was written as the error itself rather than the printed text, so those labels are read the other way round: matches means the error is real. verdict is the adjudicator's five-line verdict in the prompt's convention, the same as the runs': matches means the printed text is right, disagrees that it is wrong, can't tell that the repo can't settle it. classification a/b/c is kept for reference: a row stands, b row wrong, c can't tell. runs_right lists the runs whose substance (not label) agreed with the adjudication.
